verified_publications.title: Effectiveness and safety assessment of calcium channel blockers compared to beta blockers in patients with angina: An observational study
verified_publications.journal: Pakistan Journal of Pharmaceutical Sciences (Pak. J. Pharm. Sci.)
verified_publications.ethics_approval: IBC KU-317/2023 (Institutional Bio-ethical Research Committee, University of Karachi)
verified_publications.sample_size: N = 110 angina patients (61 male, 49 female; June 2022 - June 2023)
verified_publications.key_evidence_summary: Evaluated Beta Blockers (BB, 36.36%), Calcium Channel Blockers (CCB, 54.4%), and CCB+BB combination (9.8%) in tertiary care cardiology OPDs using Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ-7) and Naranjo ADR scale. Improved angina symptoms in 83/110 patients (p < 0.05). CCB SAQ-7 score (83.97 ± 3.18) and combination (82.64 ± 5.12) outperformed BB (80.46 ± 5.99), with CCB exhibiting fewer Definite/Probable ADRs over long-term angina control.

verified_publications.title: Evaluation of carbapenem antimicrobial stewardship program at a tertiary care hospital: A prospective interventional study
verified_publications.journal: Pakistan Journal of Pharmaceutical Sciences (Pak. J. Pharm. Sci.)
verified_publications.ethics_approval: App#0592-2020 LNH-ERC (Liaquat National Hospital Ethical Committee)
verified_publications.sample_size: N = 134 non-adherent carbapenem prescriptions in Medical ICU/HDU (Dec 2020 - May 2021)
verified_publications.key_evidence_summary: Prospective interventional study at Liaquat National Hospital evaluating physician acceptance and clinical outcomes of pharmacist-led Antimicrobial Stewardship Program (ASP) interventions for carbapenem therapy. ASP interventions were accepted in 117/134 (87.3%) patients, resulting in 7-day clinical improvement in 99 (84.6%) patients and a significant reduction in 30-day readmission due to re-infection (p = 0.036). Interventions included renal dose adjustment for creatinine clearance (62.7%, n=84) and antibiotic de-escalation (25.4%, n=34).

verified_publications.title: Evaluating knowledge of high-alert medications among nurses, pharmacists, and clinicians to improve medication safety
verified_publications.journal: Journal of Pharmaceutical Policy and Practice (Abstract 223, PESP Conference 2025 Part A)
verified_publications.ethics_approval: Liaquat National Hospital and Medical College, Karachi
verified_publications.sample_size: N = 60 healthcare professionals (20 clinicians, 20 nurses, 20 pharmacists) + 6-month HAM consumption audit
verified_publications.key_evidence_summary: Assessed hospital staff knowledge and 6-month consumption patterns (June-Nov 2024) of High-Alert Medications (HAMs), specifically electrolytes. Pharmacists achieved the highest knowledge score (80%), followed by nurses (75%) and clinicians (70%), identifying targeted gaps in drug compatibility, storage, and labeling.

verified_publications.title: AI meets human expertise: Comparision between clinical pharmacist interventions and artificial intelligence at a tertiary care hospital in Pakistan
verified_publications.journal: Journal of Pharmaceutical Policy and Practice (Abstract 225, PESP Conference 2025 Part A)
verified_publications.ethics_approval: Liaquat National Hospital and Medical College, Karachi
verified_publications.key_evidence_summary: Prospective study comparing clinical pharmacist interventions with AI (ChatGPT 4.0) across drug-drug interactions, renal-adjusted antibiotic dosing, and electrolyte imbalance management. Validated by 3 independent clinical pharmacists; demonstrated that while AI detected DDIs and electrolyte issues, human clinical pharmacists were indispensable for accurate renal-adjusted antibiotic dosing in ICU settings.
